+from typing import Iterator

+def split_graphemes(text: str) -> Iterator[str]:
+    """Split a string into its constituent grapheme clusters.
+
+    This is a simplified implementation of the Unicode grapheme cluster
+    boundary rules. It handles the most common cases including emojis
+    and combining marks.
+    """
+    if not text:
+        return
+
+    index = 0
+    length = len(text)
+    while index < length:
+        char = text[index]
+        # Start of a grapheme cluster
+        cluster = char
+        index += 1
+        while index < length:
+            next_char = text[index]
+            # Simple rule: combining marks and modifiers belong to the previous cluster
+            # This is a heuristic and doesn't cover all Unicode rules but is
+            # enough for most terminal use cases.
+            # Range for Combining Diacritical Marks: U+0300–U+036F
+            # Range for Emoji modifiers: U+1F3FB–U+1F3FF
+            # Range for Variation Selectors: U+FE00–U+FE0F
+            # Range for Zero Width Joiner: U+200D
+            cp = ord(next_char)
+            if (
+                (0x0300 <= cp <= 0x036F) or
+                (0x1F3FB <= cp <= 0x1F3FF) or
+                (0xFE00 <= cp <= 0xFE0F) or
+                (cp == 0x200D) or
+                (0x1F1E6 <= cp <= 0x1F1FF) # Regional indicator symbols

+from rich.text import Text

+def test_private_escape_sequences():
+    # \x1b7 is a private escape sequence (save cursor position)
+    # It should be stripped when using Text.from_ansi
+    input_text = "A\x1b7B"
+    result = Text.from_ansi(input_text)

+

+    input_text_0 = "C\x1b0D"
+    result_0 = Text.from_ansi(input_text_0)
+    assert str(result_0) == "CD", f"Expected 'CD', got {repr(str(result_0))}"
+    
+    # \x1b? is the upper bound of the private range
+    input_text_q = "E\x1b?F"
+    result_q = Text.from_ansi(input_text_q)
+    assert str(result_q) == "EF", f"Expected 'EF', got {repr(str(result_q))}"
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
